root_cause.text: The UFS core driver failed to flush pending exception event handling work during suspend when the runtime power management level was set to UFS_PM_LVL_0, allowing asynchronous exception handlers to access the host controller after the system entered deep power-down state.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds two critical operations (`ufshcd_disable_auto_bkops(hba)` and `flush_work(&hba->eeh_work)`) in the suspend path when `req_dev_pwr_mode == UFS_ACTIVE_PWR_MODE && req_link_state == UIC_LINK_ACTIVE_STATE`. The CVE description explicitly states that "Previously, the UFS core driver bypassed flushing exception event handling jobs in this configuration," creating a race condition where "the driver could attempt to access the host controller to handle an exception after the system had already entered a deep power-down state, resulting in a system crash." The missing `flush_work(&hba->eeh_work)` call is the direct cause of the vulnerability.

intent_record.intent_summary: Disable auto background operations and flush pending error handling work before suspending an active UFS device to prevent race conditions and ensure clean state transition.
intent_record.what: Added two function calls before the goto statement: ufshcd_disable_auto_bkops(hba) and flush_work(&hba->eeh_work) in the condition where req_dev_pwr_mode is UFS_ACTIVE_PWR_MODE and req_link_state is UIC_LINK_ACTIVE_STATE.
intent_record.how: When the UFS device is in active power mode and link is active, the code now explicitly disables automatic background operations and waits for any pending error handling work to complete before proceeding to the vops_suspend label. This ensures proper cleanup and synchronization of background tasks before suspension.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerability root cause states that the UFS core driver failed to flush pending exception event handling work during suspend when the runtime power management level was set to UFS_PM_LVL_0. Line 8775 shows `flush_work(&hba->eeh_work);` which flushes the exception event handler work. However, this flush occurs unconditionally for all power management operations. The bug is that when `pm_lvl == UFS_PM_LVL_0` (which corresponds to `req_dev_pwr_mode == UFS_ACTIVE_PWR_MODE && req_link_state == UIC_LINK_ACTIVE_STATE`), the code takes the early exit at line 8735 via `goto vops_suspend;` BEFORE reaching the `flush_work(&hba->eeh_work);` call at line 8775. This means the exception event handler work is never flushed for the UFS_PM_LVL_0 case, allowing asynchronous exception handlers to access the host controller after deep power-down. The fix would require moving the `flush_work(&hba->eeh_work);` call to before the early return at line 8735, or adding it before the vops_suspend label.
